question.text: What are the four parts of the Missouri driver examination?

answer.text: The Missouri driver examination has four parts: a written test on traffic laws and safe-driving rules, a vision test, a road sign test and a driving skills test.

teaching.text: Each part checks something different: what you know, how you see, whether you know the signs, and how you handle the car. Remember: written, vision, signs, driving.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Missouri driver examination has four parts: a written test on traffic laws and safe-driving rules, a vision test, a road sign test and a driving skills test.

question.text: In which three situations is the Missouri driver examination required?

answer.text: The examination is required for a new Missouri license, for a Missouri license expired more than six months (one hundred eighty-four days), and whenever the Director of Revenue asks, even if your license is current.

teaching.text: The examination is not only for beginners; a long expiration or a request from the Director brings it back too. Remember: new, long expired, Director asks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The examination is required for a new Missouri license, for a Missouri license expired more than six months (one hundred eighty-four days), and whenever the Director of Revenue asks, even if your license is current.

question.text: Which license revocations send a driver back through the examination?

answer.text: A license revoked for too many points or for an Administrative Alcohol action also sends the driver back through the examination.

teaching.text: Point and Administrative Alcohol revocations put the driver back at the start, facing the full examination again. Remember: points or alcohol revocation.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A license revoked for too many points or for an Administrative Alcohol action also sends the driver back through the examination.

question.text: Which out-of-state drivers take only the vision and road sign tests?

answer.text: A driver whose license from another state is valid or expired less than one hundred eighty-four days, applying for the same type of Missouri license, takes only the vision and road sign tests.

teaching.text: A recent license of the same type shows you already drive, so only vision and road signs are checked. Remember: valid transfer, two tests.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver whose license from another state is valid or expired less than one hundred eighty-four days, applying for the same type of Missouri license, takes only the vision and road sign tests.

question.text: What two conditions must an out-of-state license meet for the shortened route?

answer.text: An out-of-state license qualifies for the shortened vision and road sign route only if it is for the same type of license and is valid or expired less than one hundred eighty-four days.

teaching.text: Check both conditions before choosing the short route: the same license type, and valid or recently expired. Remember: same type, recent enough.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An out-of-state license qualifies for the shortened vision and road sign route only if it is for the same type of license and is valid or expired less than one hundred eighty-four days.

question.text: Who gives the Missouri driver examination, and who can point you to a testing center?

answer.text: The Missouri State Highway Patrol (MSHP) gives the driver examination, and either the MSHP or the Department can point you to the nearest testing center.

teaching.text: The Highway Patrol runs the examination, and the Patrol or the Department can tell you where the nearest testing center is. Remember: Highway Patrol tests.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Missouri State Highway Patrol (MSHP) gives the driver examination, and either the MSHP or the Department can point you to the nearest testing center.

question.text: What must you prove before the exam, and when do you show that identification again?

answer.text: You must prove your legal name and age before the exam, and you show that identification again whenever you apply for a license or permit and each time you take the written or driving test.

teaching.text: Bring proof of your legal name and age every time, because it is checked at each application and each test. Remember: name and age, every time.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must prove your legal name and age before the exam, and you show that identification again whenever you apply for a license or permit and each time you take the written or driving test.

question.text: Where can you find Department and Highway Patrol phone numbers and testing locations?

answer.text: The phone numbers for the Department and the Highway Patrol are printed at the back of the guide, and testing locations are also listed on the Highway Patrol website.

teaching.text: Look at the back of the guide for the phone numbers, or the Highway Patrol website for testing locations. Remember: back of the guide.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The phone numbers for the Department and the Highway Patrol are printed at the back of the guide, and testing locations are also listed on the Highway Patrol website.

question.text: What format and length does the Class F written test have?

answer.text: The Class F written test has twenty-five multiple-choice questions on the laws and driving methods this guide covers.

teaching.text: Study the whole guide, because the questions can cover any of the laws and driving methods in it. Remember: twenty-five multiple choice.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Class F written test has twenty-five multiple-choice questions on the laws and driving methods this guide covers.

question.text: Is the Class F written test open book, and is the commercial vehicle chapter on it?

answer.text: The written test is not open book, and a Class F applicant is not tested on the commercial vehicle material in Chapter fifteen.

teaching.text: Closed book means you rely on what you studied, and the commercial chapter is not on a Class F test. Remember: closed book, no commercial.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The written test is not open book, and a Class F applicant is not tested on the commercial vehicle material in Chapter fifteen.

question.text: How does the written test differ for a Class E for-hire applicant?

answer.text: A Class E for-hire applicant takes a special written test that adds the Chapter fifteen commercial vehicle material, and it is also not open book.

teaching.text: A Class E for-hire applicant has more to study, but the closed-book rule stays the same. Remember: Class E adds commercial.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Class E for-hire applicant takes a special written test that adds the Chapter fifteen commercial vehicle material, and it is also not open book.

question.text: How do the Class F and Class E written tests differ, and what do they share?

answer.text: Both the Class F and the Class E written tests are closed book; the difference is that only the Class E test includes the commercial vehicle chapter.

teaching.text: Keep the shared rule and the one difference together: both closed book, and only Class E adds commercial material. Remember: both closed, E adds commercial.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Both the Class F and the Class E written tests are closed book; the difference is that only the Class E test includes the commercial vehicle chapter.

question.text: What does the road sign test check?

answer.text: The road sign test checks whether you can recognize traffic signs and understand what they mean.

teaching.text: Study the shapes, colors and messages of signs, since the test checks both recognition and meaning. Remember: know the signs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The road sign test checks whether you can recognize traffic signs and understand what they mean.

question.text: What kinds of exam fraud are punished, and how?

answer.text: Fraud in any license, permit or nondriver ID examination, such as false statements, cheating, or using a recording, camera or two-way communication device, is a Class A misdemeanor that can cost your driving privilege for up to one year.

teaching.text: Cheating, false statements or using a camera or two-way device can cost your driving privilege for up to a year. Remember: cheating is a misdemeanor.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Fraud in any license, permit or nondriver ID examination, such as false statements, cheating, or using a recording, camera or two-way communication device, is a Class A misdemeanor that can cost your driving privilege for up to one year.

question.text: Which two vision tests does every new or renewal applicant take?

answer.text: Every new or renewal license or permit applicant takes both an acuity test and a peripheral (side) vision test.

teaching.text: Think of the vision test as two tests: one for sharpness and one for side vision. Remember: sharpness and side vision.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every new or renewal license or permit applicant takes both an acuity test and a peripheral (side) vision test.

question.text: What is the standard minimum acuity for a Missouri license?

answer.text: The standard minimum acuity is twenty or forty or better using either eye or both eyes.

teaching.text: Twenty forty is the level to aim for, using either eye or both eyes together. Remember: twenty forty or better.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The standard minimum acuity is twenty or forty or better using either eye or both eyes.

question.text: Does passing the acuity screen also cover side vision?

answer.text: The twenty or forty figure is the standard passing acuity, while a separate peripheral test measures side vision, so passing one screen does not cover the other.

teaching.text: A driver with sharp eyes can still fall short on side vision, so each screen must be passed on its own. Remember: two separate screens.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The twenty or forty figure is the standard passing acuity, while a separate peripheral test measures side vision, so passing one screen does not cover the other.

question.text: What is the standard minimum side vision for a Missouri license?

answer.text: The standard minimum side vision is fifty-five degrees or more in each eye, or eighty-five degrees or more in one eye.

teaching.text: Side vision has two ways to pass: both eyes at the lower level, or one eye at the higher level. Remember: fifty-five each, eighty-five one.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The standard minimum side vision is fifty-five degrees or more in each eye, or eighty-five degrees or more in one eye.

question.text: What are the two passing routes for side vision, and what is the floor below which no license is possible?

answer.text: Side vision has two passing routes, fifty-five degrees in each eye or eighty-five degrees in a single eye, while seventy degrees combined is the floor below which no license is possible.

teaching.text: The two passing routes are standards, while seventy degrees combined is the floor below which no license is possible. Remember: fifty-five, eighty-five, seventy floor.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Side vision has two passing routes, fifty-five degrees in each eye or eighty-five degrees in a single eye, while seventy degrees combined is the floor below which no license is possible.

question.text: What can happen if you miss the vision standards?

answer.text: Missing the vision standards can lead to a denied license or to restrictions placed on the license.

teaching.text: A missed standard does not always mean no license; restrictions are one possible outcome. Remember: denial or restrictions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Missing the vision standards can lead to a denied license or to restrictions placed on the license.

question.text: What happens if you fail the standard vision test at the exam?

answer.text: If you fail the standard vision test, the examiner hands you a vision exam form for an eye specialist or physician, and a new prescription may mean waiting for the glasses or contacts before the written or driving test.

teaching.text: A failed screen sends you to an eye specialist, and new glasses may mean waiting before the other tests. Remember: form for the eye doctor.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you fail the standard vision test, the examiner hands you a vision exam form for an eye specialist or physician, and a new prescription may mean waiting for the glasses or contacts before the written or driving test.

question.text: Below which vision levels can you neither take the driving test nor hold a Missouri license?

answer.text: If both natural and corrected acuity are worse than twenty or one hundred sixty, or combined side vision is worse than seventy degrees, you cannot take the driving test or hold a Missouri license.

teaching.text: These are floors, not passing levels; below them, no Missouri license is possible at all. Remember: twenty one-sixty, seventy combined.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If both natural and corrected acuity are worse than twenty or one hundred sixty, or combined side vision is worse than seventy degrees, you cannot take the driving test or hold a Missouri license.

question.text: Is twenty or one hundred sixty the standard passing acuity?

answer.text: The twenty or one hundred sixty acuity cutoff applies only when both natural and corrected vision are worse than it; it is the point at which a license is impossible, not the standard passing level.

teaching.text: Do not confuse the cutoff with the standard: twenty forty passes, and the lower figure rules out any license. Remember: cutoff, not passing level.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The twenty or one hundred sixty acuity cutoff applies only when both natural and corrected vision are worse than it; it is the point at which a license is impossible, not the standard passing level.

question.text: When is the driving test given, and by whom?

answer.text: The driving test comes only after the written, vision and road sign tests are passed, and it is given by an MSHP driver license examiner.

teaching.text: The driving test is the last step, given only after the knowledge and vision parts are behind you. Remember: driving test comes last.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The driving test comes only after the written, vision and road sign tests are passed, and it is given by an MSHP driver license examiner.

question.text: What does the examiner check about the test vehicle, and when is the test refused?

answer.text: The examiner inspects the test vehicle for required equipment and safe condition, and the test is refused if the vehicle is not properly equipped or testing seems dangerous.

teaching.text: Check your own car before test day, because an unsafe or poorly equipped car ends the attempt before it starts. Remember: unsafe car, no test.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The examiner inspects the test vehicle for required equipment and safe condition, and the test is refused if the vehicle is not properly equipped or testing seems dangerous.

question.text: Which plates, sticker, belts, doors and seat does the test vehicle need?

answer.text: The test vehicle needs current plates, a valid inspection sticker, working seat belts, working doors for the driver and the examiner, and a clean, safe passenger seat.

teaching.text: Go through this list at home, since a missing sticker or a stuck door is enough for a refusal. Remember: plates, sticker, belts, doors.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The test vehicle needs current plates, a valid inspection sticker, working seat belts, working doors for the driver and the examiner, and a clean, safe passenger seat.

question.text: Which brakes, warning device and paperwork must the test vehicle also have?

answer.text: The test vehicle also needs a working parking brake and foot brake, a working horn, and proof of financial responsibility.

teaching.text: The brakes, the horn and proof of financial responsibility finish the equipment list. Remember: brakes, horn, insurance proof.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The test vehicle also needs a working parking brake and foot brake, a working horn, and proof of financial responsibility.

question.text: Who rides during the driving test, and how should you behave?

answer.text: Only you and the examiner ride during the test; skip needless conversation, remember the examiner is there to test rather than teach, and obey every Missouri traffic law.

teaching.text: The examiner is there to test you, not to coach you, so keep conversation to a minimum and follow every traffic law. Remember: examiner tests, not teaches.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Only you and the examiner ride during the test; skip needless conversation, remember the examiner is there to test rather than teach, and obey every Missouri traffic law.

question.text: After the examiner gives a direction, how much time do you have?

answer.text: After the examiner gives a direction, you are allowed enough time to check traffic and carry it out.

teaching.text: There is no need to rush; you are given time to check traffic before you carry out each direction. Remember: time to check first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After the examiner gives a direction, you are allowed enough time to check traffic and carry it out.

question.text: When asked to use a control such as the wipers, what are you graded on?

answer.text: When asked to use controls such as the accelerator, brakes, turn signals and wipers, you are graded on finding each one without searching and using it correctly.

teaching.text: Practice in the car you will use on test day so you can find every control without searching. Remember: find it, use it right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When asked to use controls such as the accelerator, brakes, turn signals and wipers, you are graded on finding each one without searching and using it correctly.

question.text: What are you graded on when you pull away from the curb?

answer.text: When you pull away you are graded on starting the car, releasing the parking brake, checking that the way is clear, signaling, and driving smoothly at the right speed.

teaching.text: Forgetting the parking brake or the signal costs points right at the start of the test. Remember: start, release, check, signal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When you pull away you are graded on starting the car, releasing the parking brake, checking that the way is clear, signaling, and driving smoothly at the right speed.

question.text: How are starting and stopping graded?

answer.text: Starting and stopping are graded for smoothness and safety, reaction time and control of the car while stopping.

teaching.text: Smooth, well-timed starts and stops show the examiner that you are in control of the car. Remember: smooth, quick, controlled.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Starting and stopping are graded for smoothness and safety, reaction time and control of the car while stopping.

question.text: How large is the space used for the parallel parking task?

answer.text: The parallel parking task uses a space twenty-five feet long and seven feet wide.

teaching.text: The marked space is part of what makes parallel parking different from the hill task. Remember: twenty-five by seven.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The parallel parking task uses a space twenty-five feet long and seven feet wide.

question.text: What curb distance, position and time limit are scored in parallel parking?

answer.text: Parallel parking is scored on stopping no more than eighteen inches from the curb, near the middle of the space, and finishing within two minutes.

teaching.text: Distance, position and time are all scored, so practice until all three feel natural. Remember: eighteen inches, two minutes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parallel parking is scored on stopping no more than eighteen inches from the curb, near the middle of the space, and finishing within two minutes.

question.text: Besides distance and time, what else is scored in parallel parking?

answer.text: Parallel parking is also scored on your position before backing, not touching the space markers, turning the wheels the right way, and checking traffic and signaling before pulling out.

teaching.text: Technique counts too: where you start, the markers, the wheel turns, and checking and signaling to leave. Remember: markers, wheels, signal out.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parallel parking is also scored on your position before backing, not touching the space markers, turning the wheels the right way, and checking traffic and signaling before pulling out.

question.text: Which parking task has a time limit and a marked space?

answer.text: Only parallel parking carries a time limit, two minutes, and only it uses a marked space, twenty-five feet long by seven feet wide.

teaching.text: Only parallel parking has a clock and a marked space; hill parking has neither. Remember: only parallel is timed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Only parallel parking carries a time limit, two minutes, and only it uses a marked space, twenty-five feet long by seven feet wide.

question.text: How must you look and drive when backing on the test?

answer.text: When backing, you look over your right shoulder through the rear window and must keep a straight line, stay in the proper lane and hold the right speed.

teaching.text: Looking over your right shoulder through the rear window keeps the backing straight and in the proper lane. Remember: right shoulder, straight line.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When backing, you look over your right shoulder through the rear window and must keep a straight line, stay in the proper lane and hold the right speed.

question.text: How many turns do you make on the test, and what is graded?

answer.text: You make at least two right turns and two left turns, graded on lane choice, timely signals, turning into the proper lane, traffic checks, speed and control.

teaching.text: Each turn is several small tasks: lane choice, signal, traffic check, proper lane, speed and control. Remember: two right, two left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You make at least two right turns and two left turns, graded on lane choice, timely signals, turning into the proper lane, traffic checks, speed and control.

question.text: What is the minimum number of each kind of turn on the test?

answer.text: For the turning task you make a minimum of two right and two left turns.

teaching.text: Expect at least two turns each way, so practice both directions equally. Remember: two and two.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For the turning task you make a minimum of two right and two left turns.

question.text: What is scored when you park on a hill during the test?

answer.text: Parking on a hill is graded on stopping no more than eighteen inches from the curb, leaving the car in park or the correct gear, turning the front wheels correctly, setting the parking brake, then checking traffic and signaling.

teaching.text: These are the same hill habits from the parking chapter, now scored by an examiner. Remember: eighteen inches, wheels, brake.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parking on a hill is graded on stopping no more than eighteen inches from the curb, leaving the car in park or the correct gear, turning the front wheels correctly, setting the parking brake, then checking traffic and signaling.

question.text: What curb-distance limit do parallel parking and hill parking share?

answer.text: Parallel parking and hill parking use the same curb-distance limit of no more than eighteen inches.

teaching.text: The one limit both parking tasks share is the curb distance. Remember: eighteen inches both.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parallel parking and hill parking use the same curb-distance limit of no more than eighteen inches.

question.text: What are you graded on at intersections?

answer.text: At intersections you are graded on obeying signs and lights, approach speed, awareness of traffic, lane position, yielding without blocking traffic, and a full stop at the proper place for stop signs.

teaching.text: Approach and passage both count, from speed and lane before the intersection to yielding and stopping in it. Remember: signs, speed, yield, stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At intersections you are graded on obeying signs and lights, approach speed, awareness of traffic, lane position, yielding without blocking traffic, and a full stop at the proper place for stop signs.

question.text: Which two intersection behaviors are singled out in the intersection task?

answer.text: The intersection task includes making a full stop at the proper place at stop signs and yielding without blocking other traffic.

teaching.text: A rolling stop is not a full stop, even when the cross street is empty. Remember: full stop, yield clear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The intersection task includes making a full stop at the proper place at stop signs and yielding without blocking other traffic.

question.text: What does the examiner watch throughout the whole test?

answer.text: Throughout the test the examiner also watches your following distance, speed, lane use and lane markings, traffic awareness and yielding.

teaching.text: The examiner grades everyday habits between tasks, not only the set maneuvers. Remember: distance, speed, lanes, yielding.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Throughout the test the examiner also watches your following distance, speed, lane use and lane markings, traffic awareness and yielding.

question.text: What does the examiner grade about traffic signs and signals throughout the drive?

answer.text: The examiner also grades whether you notice and obey traffic signs and signals throughout the drive.

teaching.text: Missing a sign on a quiet stretch can cost as much as a mistake during a maneuver. Remember: notice and obey.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The examiner also grades whether you notice and obey traffic signs and signals throughout the drive.

question.text: How does the point system decide a failed driving test?

answer.text: The examiner deducts points for driving errors, and losing more than thirty points fails the driving test.

teaching.text: Small errors add up, so the aim is to drive well enough that few points are lost. Remember: over thirty points fails.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The examiner deducts points for driving errors, and losing more than thirty points fails the driving test.

question.text: Which errors fail the driving test at once?

answer.text: You fail at once for an at-fault crash with another vehicle, hitting a pedestrian, driving so dangerously a crash could have resulted, breaking a traffic law, or refusing to drive as directed.

teaching.text: These serious errors end the test immediately, whatever your point total. Remember: crash, pedestrian, danger, law.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You fail at once for an at-fault crash with another vehicle, hitting a pedestrian, driving so dangerously a crash could have resulted, breaking a traffic law, or refusing to drive as directed.

question.text: Can you fail the driving test without reaching the point limit?

answer.text: A test can be failed outright without reaching the point limit, for example by breaking a traffic law or refusing an instruction.

teaching.text: Treat every traffic law as a pass or fail rule during the test. Remember: instant fail possible.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A test can be failed outright without reaching the point limit, for example by breaking a traffic law or refusing an instruction.

question.text: What do you receive for passing, and can you drive on it?

answer.text: Passing earns a test results form, but that form is not valid for driving; you must first apply for and receive a license at a license office.

teaching.text: Plan for a licensed driver to take you to the license office, since the results form does not let you drive. Remember: results form, not license.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing earns a test results form, but that form is not valid for driving; you must first apply for and receive a license at a license office.

question.text: How many driving tests may you take in one day?

answer.text: Only one driving test may be taken per day, and the examiner will suggest practice before a retest.

teaching.text: A failure means coming back another day, and the examiner's advice tells you what to practice. Remember: one test a day.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Only one driving test may be taken per day, and the examiner will suggest practice before a retest.

question.text: What is required after three failed driving tests?

answer.text: After three failed driving tests, no further test is allowed without written Department authorization, and you must complete extra behind-the-wheel training, send proof, and receive approval to test.

teaching.text: Three failures lead to extra behind-the-wheel practice and approval before the next attempt. Remember: three fails, extra training.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After three failed driving tests, no further test is allowed without written Department authorization, and you must complete extra behind-the-wheel training, send proof, and receive approval to test.

question.text: How do the point limit and the failure count differ?

answer.text: The point limit and the failure count are different numbers: losing more than thirty points fails a single test, while three failed tests trigger the Department authorization and extra training requirement.

teaching.text: Think of the larger number as points within one drive and the smaller one as attempts across separate days. Remember: thirty points, three tests.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The point limit and the failure count are different numbers: losing more than thirty points fails a single test, while three failed tests trigger the Department authorization and extra training requirement.

question.text: Where do failed driving test results go, and what follows?

answer.text: Results of failed driving tests are sent to the Department of Revenue, which then mails a letter requiring additional behind-the-wheel training.

teaching.text: The Department learns of each failed test and sends the letter that requires extra training. Remember: results to the Department.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Results of failed driving tests are sent to the Department of Revenue, which then mails a letter requiring additional behind-the-wheel training.

question.text: Who must give the extra training after three failures, and what is needed before the next attempt?

answer.text: The extra training after three failures must be given by an eligible driver, and you must hold Department approval to test before the next attempt.

teaching.text: The training must come from an eligible driver, and approval is needed before you may test again. Remember: eligible driver, then approval.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The extra training after three failures must be given by an eligible driver, and you must hold Department approval to test before the next attempt.
